title: Session 2 — Participant 50 User + Claude Behavior Graphs
goal: Build a reusable library of AI-assisted SOP prompts for my core recurring daily tasks in Sales & Marketing Ops — daily status reporting, client email triage, call recaps, CRM hygiene checks, and partner sync documentation — so each task can be run consistently and quickly from a saved prompt rather than rebuilt from scratch every time.
context: In Session 1, I tested Claude on one complete workflow, a single client call, from company record to follow-up email. For Session 2, I want to shift focus from running one workflow once to building reusable prompt templates for tasks I already repeat every day, so the value isn't a single output but a standing SOP I can reuse going forward. This makes Session 2 different from Session 1 in kind: Session 1 tested whether Claude could execute an end-to-end task well; Session 2 tests whether Claude can help me design a prompt that stays consistent across different inputs each time I reuse it, which is closer to my actual day-to-day use. I'd rate it similar in difficulty to Session 1, maybe slightly easier since I'm building on formats and habits I already know, but it adds the challenge of proving the prompt holds up across multiple different inputs, not just one. Being asked to use AI throughout the exercise pushed me to name the repetitive parts of my job as distinct, demoable tasks. Some of this is already my natural workflow (I already draft daily updates and check threads by hand); what's new is turning that habit into a saved, reusable AI prompt instead of rebuilding it from scratch each time.

Step 1.step_name: Build a Daily Status Update SOP Prompt
Step 1.step_action: Take a day's worth of scattered notes (calls handled, HubSpot updates, emails flagged) and work with Claude to build one reusable prompt that consistently turns them into the required plain-text, Slack-ready daily update format. Test it against a real day's activity and refine the wording until no manual reformatting is needed.
